From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Recap: LumenHealth eval plan & Redwood setup

Hi Kelly / Rahul —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: evaluate candidate models for clinical triage assistant use case (summarization of patient messages, intent classification for routing, short-response drafting).
- Key constraints: must avoid exposing PHI during evals; need reproducible scoring so vendor comparisons are defensible; target latency <= 250ms median for inference path.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist)
- Candidate models to benchmark: redwood-7b-q4 (fast, quantized), redwood-3b-32k (higher-context), open-llama-13b (baseline for accuracy).
- Eval types: automated accuracy/EM/F1 for classification, ROUGE/ROUGE-L + chrF for summarization, embedding-based semantic similarity (sentence-transformer cosine) for open responses, and manual spot checks for safety/regression.

Customer-specific eval plan (high level)
1) You provide a de-identified sample dataset (CSV, see attached prompt set) with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, label (if classification), pii_flag. We typically start with 200–500 rows for initial benchmarking.
2) We run baseline passes on the three candidate models in Redwood hosted environment and produce: per-example outputs, token-level cost and latency breakdown, aggregate metrics + failure cases.
3) We generate a short qualitative report with flagged safety/regression concerns and recommended prompt/temperature presets.

Security/PII handling
- If you prefer, we can run the evals inside your VPC via Redwood Private (we'll coordinate a Private Eval session). Otherwise, sample data should be de-identified before upload. We will provide a data-handling checklist before any transfer.

Proposed next steps
- Kelly: confirm you can share a de-identified CSV (200–500 rows) and whether you want the run in-hosted or Private.
- Rahul: if you prefer Private evals, please share the contact for infra to discuss networking.
- We: Nikhil will send a short eval quickstart + rubric and an example results CSV; then we schedule a 30-minute follow-up in one week to review findings.

Attachments: lumen_eval_promptset_v1.csv (sample format), redwood_eval_quickstart.pdf (how-to + rubric)

Thanks — happy to adjust if there were any misunderstandings from the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi Kelly —

Quick follow-up with concrete steps and the rubric you asked for. Putting this here so it's easy to copy into your QA doc.

1) Dataset format (CSV)- Required columns: id, prompt, expected_response, label (optional), pii_flag (Y/N), source_note- For summarization rows: put the full patient message in `prompt` and the clinician-ready summary in `expected_response`.

2) Submission options- Preferred: share a Drive/S3 presigned link to the CSV.- Alternative: upload to Redwood secure uploads via the console (we can generate a one-time token).

3) Eval types and scoring (we'll run these automatically and provide per-example outputs):
- Classification: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrix (per-class). Exact match for strict labels; token-level F1 for partial matches.
- Summarization: ROUGE-1/2/L, chrF, and embedding cosine (sentence-transformer) for semantic similarity.
- Free-text responses: BLEU + embedding-based ranking; we also compute a safety score which flags hallucination-like outputs using heuristics + model-based safety classifier.

Scoring rubric (short):
- Primary metric by task: classification -> Macro-F1; summarization -> ROUGE-L + embedding cosine (>=0.85 considered good for our benchmarks); drafting -> human pass rate + semantic similarity threshold.
- Regression checks: compare model candidate outputs to your current production baseline (if any) on the same dataset; report delta per metric and list top 20 degraded examples.

4) Models we suggest running initially (we'll run these unless you request others):
- redwood-7b-q4 (recommended start for latency/cost balance)
- redwood-3b-32k (for longer context needs)
- open-llama-13b (accuracy baseline/openness)

5) Example run config (we'll translate this to the Redwood eval job; shown as flat text for your QA team):
- batch_size: 8
- max_tokens: task-dependent (summaries 200, classification 64)
- temperature: 0.0 for deterministic evals; 0.7 for creative drafting tests
- top_p: 0.95
- num_samples: 1

6) Deliverables and timing
- Initial run (3 models) on 300 rows: 24–36 hours after we receive data and access (hosted).
- Private/VPC run: depends on networking setup; estimate 48–72 hours for environment prep plus 24 hours for runs.
- Deliverables: per-model CSV with outputs, metrics summary, latency/cost breakdown, top 50 failure cases with annotations, and a short recommendations doc.

7) Security notes
- Hosted retention policy for eval artefacts: default 30 days; can be shortened on request. We can also run ephemeral jobs with no persistent storage for sensitive datasets.

Attachments: redwood_eval_quickstart.pdf (includes the rubric and example result CSV). Also linking a public benchmark we've run on similar datasets: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/public/lumenhealth-similarity-results

If this looks good I'll create the Private Eval request template and send it to Rahul/your infra contact.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
